newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBJ says regrets rating cut by Moody's.
newsitem.headline: IBJ says regrets rating cut by Moody's.

text.p: The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) said on Thursday it deeply regrets the latest cut in the top Japanese bank's bond and long-term debt ratings to A2 from A1 by Moody's Investors Service.

"It is extremely regrettable that our ratings have been cut by focusing only on vague worries over the future and without fully taking into account any positive side. We can hardly accept this," IBJ said in a statement.
"We will actively cope with ongoing deregulation and prove with results that our bank can a winner in the 'Big Bang' reforms."

Earlier, Moody's said it had cut IBJ's bond and long-term debt ratings to A2 from A1. The rating firm said the advantages of IBJ's main funding vehicle, long-term debentures, will decline over time as Japanese investors are presented with a broader range of long-term fixed-income securities issued by a variety of institutions.
Moody's meanwhile confirmed IBJ's C bank financial strength rating and its Prime-1 rating for short-term deposits.
IBJ said its business base has been strengthened under ongoing financial liberalisation and that it has no problems with raising funds through debentures as Moody's said it does.
"The concerns raised by Moody's are vague assumptions and lack evidence," IBJ said.
The bank also said it was also preparing to enter new business areas such as stock underwriting and derivatives, adding it expected to be successful in the new fields.

The rating cut, which was announced just before midday in Tokyo, failed to undermine IBJ's shares on the Tokyo bourse, where they ended the session up 30 yen at 1,830 in a turnover of 5.17 million shares.
